rv.q: It is thoroughly earned and appropriate, capturing what by now feels like a deeply reciprocal relationship between a show and its audience.
But Strayed's advice knocks you down with its avalanche of kindness.
This well-staged adaptation, starring Nia Vardalos and directed by Thomas Kail (“Hamilton”), will attract the popular writer’s many fans...
Thus lacking intrinsic momentum, the show's 90 minutes can't help but unreel a bit stuporously, despite Kail's typically careful balancing of tempo and tone.
She says we should “keep the faith,” but it’s just too sappy to be theatrical.

By the time the seemingly interminable proceedings reach their conclusion, you'll be mentally dictating your own letter to Sugar, asking how to erase the memory of monotonous evenings in the theater like this one.
What is harder to communicate is how unbearably moving Narciso and Vardalos made these recitations.

Audiences experience the breathtaking honesty and wisdom that won the columnist a cultishly devoted readership, watching Strayed search her archive of sorrow, addiction, wit, horror, and growth until she lands on just the right memory to motivate, inspire, or encourage.

Vardalos' warm, funny and endearing TINY BEAUTIFUL THINGS, adapted from the same-named book of collected advice columns written for the literary website The Rumpus by Cheryl Strayed under the pen name Sugar.
Tiny Beautiful Things captures its subject succinctly and effectively.
I'm all for Sugar -- but maybe not on an Off Broadway stage.
Sadly, that's exactly what most of Tiny Beautiful Things feels like.
The question-and-answer cycle quickly becomes repetitive and makes for a long and strained 80 minutes that could probably be better spent perusing Strayed’s original columns.
2016 is coming to an end, so it’s safe to say that “Things,” adapted, co-conceived, and performed by Nia Vardalos of “My Big Fat Greek Wedding” fame, is the goopiest play of the year.
This show hits us like waves in the ocean, huge intense moments of surprising power, followed by a lull as we wait for the next.
I admired all the good intentions, but I found the effort ultimately misguided.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this advice column adaptation: some find it deeply moving and emotionally powerful, while others dismiss it as messy, sappy, and ill-suited for the stage despite strong performances.
